### 6. Problem tree from the visible materials
- Root: cancellation refund. Hop 1 (state-derived): cancellation_refund_disbursement "A cancellation refund is fixed only after the policy shows the cancellation processed on the signed request, cancelled with its cancellation effective date set." Policy status in_force -> unmet; the write that makes the policy "cancelled ... with its cancellation effective date" is described in cancellation_processing ("ends the policy on the cancellation effective date and leaves it cancelled").
- Hop 2 (state-derived): cancellation_processing "A cancellation is not processed until no claim on the policy is open, every coverage measured on the latest adjuster report for each date of loss on the policy carrying a payment or a written denial for that date of loss dated after that report." Latest report SUPPLEMENTAL 10-08 measures contents; no contents payment/denial after it -> open. Writes that bring "a payment ... dated after that report": contents_claim_payment (issues a contents payment item dated today); a written denial would need a denial reason, none supported by the records (contents measured above deductible, POL timely).
- Hop 3 (state-derived): contents_claim_payment "A contents payment on a claim is fixed only after the claim file carries a signed and sworn contents proof of loss received after the claim's latest adjuster report that measures a contents loss." Last contents POL 09-15 < 10-08 -> unmet; the write is contents_proof_of_loss (customer's own sworn statement, user tool).
- Order: contents POL (customer) -> contents payment -> process cancellation -> disburse refund. Four problems, three edges, one customer write.
- Counter-proof "do only the refund": disbursing on an in_force policy contradicts hop 1; processing at once contradicts hop 2; paying contents without a new POL contradicts hop 3 (and proof_of_loss_requirements caps payments at the sworn amount).
- Alternatives excluded: effective date = request receipt (excluded: building sold uses the event date); denial instead of payment (no visible denial ground); payee LENDER_ESCROW (payor INSURED, "paid by check").
- Hop marks: all state-derived. Note for 3b: cancellation_risk_premium_credit §4 "A policy with an open claim is not cancelled until every claim on it is closed" restates hop 2 inside the processing policy's computation document; cancellation_refund_working §B "the risk premium credit is booked when the cancellation is processed ... when the refund is disbursed" names processing beside the refund rule. Neither handed me the hop (I derived each from the hub sentence and the records), but they are judged in dependency_form.
